title: YOURLS
name: yourls
description: URL shortener you run yourself: short links on your own address with custom keywords, click stats with referrers and countries, bookmarklets and an API for making links from scripts. Source: https://github.com/YOURLS/YOURLS

env.name: YOURLS_URL
env.label: Address you'll open it on (required)
env.description: Exactly what you'll type in the browser, port included, all lowercase and no slash at the end, like http://192.168.1.20:8400. Every short link and admin page is built from it.

env.name: YOURLS_ADMIN_PASSWORD
env.label: Admin password (required)
env.description: What you'll log in to the admin area with.

note: Fill in the address, admin password and database password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them. The address has to be exactly what you'll type in the browser, like http://192.168.1.20:8400: the port you're using, all lowercase, and no slash at the end. YOURLS builds every short link, page and button from it, so if it's wrong the short links it hands out point at that address, and the admin pages load without styling and can't shorten anything. To fix it, change the address in the stack's environment variables and redeploy. Then open /admin on that address (the bare address just says Forbidden, that's normal), click Install YOURLS once to set up the database, and log in with the admin username and password from the form. The password stays in the stack's environment variables, so that's where you change it. The install adds three sample links to yourls.org, delete them if you like. Short links are public, and so are their stats pages (add a + to any short link), which draw their charts with Google Charts. The admin list also shows each site's icon from Google. For scripts, use the signature token under Tools rather than your password. Links and stats live in the db-data volume. Docs: yourls.org/docs
